name: wait_cia_flag_after_call
description: Calls a routine through a library jump vector with a 512-byte size, then loops while bit 6 of the CIA-A port register is set, so it waits on the fire-button or disk status line. Text referenced: FUCK, spcrus.sav.

name: copy_128_longs_to_buffer
description: Copies 128 longwords from the caller's source pointer into a global buffer, then calls the routine that waits on the CIA flag. Text referenced: FUCK.

name: save_buffer_unless_marker_set
description: Compares a global longword with the ASCII tag FUCK; if it differs, copies the 128-longword global buffer out to the caller's pointer. When the tag matches, it returns with the high result half set to minus one.

name: return_minus_one_high_word
description: Returns its single argument as the low 32-bit half of the result and sets the high 32-bit half to minus one.

name: return_data_register_unchanged
description: Returns the current value of the data register without modifying it, so it acts as a pass-through.

name: rotate_invert_check_byte
description: Rotates the low byte of the data register right by one bit and inverts it, then loops forever if the result differs from a global byte; otherwise it returns that byte.

name: spin_forever_stub
description: Contains only an endless loop and never returns, so calling it leaves the program stuck in place.

name: unrecovered_short_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this seven-instruction routine, so its behaviour is not recovered. It is called by one routine and calls nothing.

name: patch_jumps_when_call_fails
description: Sets a global to the character 1 and makes a library vector call with two arguments. If that call returns a negative value, it writes jump instructions into two memory slots that point to an unnamed routine; text referenced: disk.

name: copy_blocks_then_jump
description: Copies longword blocks of four from a source pointer to a destination pointer until a 16-bit counter wraps. It then writes jump opcodes into two fixed memory locations, calls through a library vector, and performs an indirect jump; calls two other routines.

name: report_call_result_via_library
description: Calls an unnamed routine, then, if a flag argument is nonzero, stores a digit character in a global and calls a library vector. It returns the result when it is nonnegative and its bitwise complement otherwise; text referenced: disk.

name: return_complemented_data_register
description: Returns a 64-bit value whose high half is the bitwise complement of the data register and whose low half is the first stack argument.

name: stub_returns_immediately
description: Contains no instructions beyond returning, so calling it does nothing.

name: store_digit_and_call_library
description: If a flag word is nonzero, stores the character 1 plus the data register value in a global and calls a library vector with the result. It returns that value when nonnegative and its complement otherwise; text referenced: disk.

name: return_complement_with_stack_arg
description: Returns a 64-bit value whose high half is the bitwise complement of the data register and whose low half is the first stack argument.

name: relocate_code_then_jump
description: Copies 256 longwords from its own code into a fixed buffer in memory, then jumps into that buffer through an indirect call. Calls one other routine.

name: boot_setup_copper_and_jump
description: Disables custom-chip interrupts, clears a bit of the CIA-B port register, and points both copper list pointers at a memory location. It calls routines that poll the CIA-A flag bit 4, then performs an indirect jump through a stored vector; hardware registers touched: CIAA_PRA, CIAB_PRA, COLOR00, COP1LCH, COP2LCH, INTENA.

name: store_vector_then_jump
description: Stores a vector into a memory slot, then repeatedly calls routines and clears a byte until a 16-bit counter reaches a fixed value. It then performs an indirect jump through the stored vector; calls two other routines.

name: repeat_clear_then_jump
description: Repeatedly calls routines and clears a byte until a 16-bit counter reaches a fixed value, then performs an indirect jump through a stored vector. Calls three other routines.

name: count_bytes_then_poll_flag
description: Increments a byte until it reaches 11, then increments a 16-bit counter. On every second pass it sets a bit in the CIA-B port register, writes two byte values to memory, and polls a status byte until its low bit is set; calls an empty routine and two other routines.

name: start_disk_read_with_retries
description: Programs the disk controller with the standard MFM sync word, a DMA pointer and a transfer length, then polls the disk status bit with a bounded retry loop. On success it sets a global to 2 and writes the disk-block interrupt request; otherwise it repeats the attempt; hardware registers touched: ADKCON, CIAA_PRA, CIAB_PRA, DSKLEN, DSKPTH, DSKSYNC, INTREQ, INTREQR.

name: find_sync_and_read_sector
description: Scans a buffer for the disk sync word, skipping repeated sync words, and checks a sector identifier byte from an unnamed routine until it matches a global. It then copies 128 longwords, produced by repeatedly calling an unnamed routine, into the destination pointer.

name: match_sector_then_store_block
description: Repeatedly calls an unnamed routine and scans for the disk sync word until its result matches a byte in a control block. It then stores 128 longwords from an unnamed routine at the block's destination pointer and advances that pointer.

name: fill_block_from_routine
description: Stores 128 longwords, each produced by calling an unnamed routine, at the destination pointer held in a control block, and then advances that pointer.

name: combine_masked_pointer_bits
description: Returns the data register ANDed with the longword at the second pointer, ORed with the data register ANDed with the first pointer's longword shifted left by one bit.

name: write_byte_pair_and_poll
description: Sets a bit in the CIA-B port register, writes two fixed byte values to two memory locations, and polls a status byte until its low bit is set. Calls one other routine.

name: write_word_bytes_then_poll
description: Writes the low and high bytes of the data register word to two consecutive memory locations, then polls a status byte until its low bit is set.

name: mask_byte_and_store_value
description: Keeps the top two bits of one memory byte, sets its bit 3, and writes the value 127 to a second memory byte.

description: Configures interrupt and DMA control, the display window, data fetch range, bitplane modulo and control registers, then calls a helper routine many times with address-like values, apparently to build a copper list. name: process_twelve_byte_records
description: Computes the address of a 12-byte record from its index argument and visits two consecutive records. For each one whose 16-bit field is nonnegative, it calls an unnamed routine.

name: process_twelve_byte_records
description: Computes the address of a 12-byte record from its index argument and visits two consecutive records. For each one whose 16-bit field is nonnegative, it calls an unnamed routine.

name: forward_call_to_routine

description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no other effect.

name: copy_strided_word_block
description: Copies five passes of 40 word pairs from a source address derived from its index argument into a destination whose rows are 10240 bytes apart. Each pass advances the destination by 40 bytes per pair.

name: combine_masked_source_tables
description: Combines two source tables into a destination in groups of five longwords. For each group it ANDs the destination with one source table and then ORs in a second source table, repeated over several passes.

name: and_or_combine_two_longs
description: Combines two source tables into a destination in groups of two longwords. For each group it ANDs the destination with one source table and then ORs in a second source table, over five passes.

name: and_or_combine_words
description: Combines two source tables into a destination using an AND followed by an OR, reading one longword and one word per group with a six-byte source stride, over several passes.

name: shift_and_merge_source_words
description: Shifts source words by a bit offset derived from its arguments. It ANDs the destination with a shifted, ones-extended source word and then ORs in a shifted data word from a second source, repeated over several passes; called by four unnamed routines.

name: fade_palette_entries_down
description: For each of 32 colour words, reduces each of its three 4-bit colour channels by one toward zero, skipping entries that are zero. It stores the result in the global palette and in a second table.

name: increment_palette_channels_to_target
description: Repeats an unnamed routine call fifteen times. Each pass compares 32 colour words with a target palette and increments every 4-bit channel that differs from its target, storing the results in the global palette and a second table.

name: spin_while_argument_nonzero
description: Loops with no body while its word argument is nonzero, so a nonzero argument never returns. It is called by three unnamed routines.

name: copy_forty_byte_rows
description: Copies rows of 40 bytes, ten longwords each, from a source buffer into a destination with a 10240-byte row stride. The row count comes from its word argument, and the copy repeats over five passes.

name: clear_large_longword_block
description: Writes zero longwords in a loop of 28 per pass for about 457 passes, then writes four more zero longwords at the end.

name: swap_buffers_after_flag
description: Waits until a global flag byte becomes nonzero, swaps two global longword pointers as a double-buffer exchange, clears the flag, and calls an unnamed routine.

name: clear_two_sixteen_long_tables
description: Zeroes sixteen longwords in each of two destinations, one a global and the other at an offset from a base register.

name: vblank_handler_flip_bitplanes
description: Vertical-blank interrupt handler: it reads the interrupt request register, and when the vertical-blank bit is set it increments a frame counter, calls a routine, and writes four bitplane pointers spaced 10240 bytes apart. Hardware registers touched: BPL1PTH, INTREQ, INTREQR.

name: dispatch_indexed_routine_call
description: If its word argument is within a limit held in a global, it returns. Otherwise it looks up a word offset in a table by that index and calls the routine it addresses.

name: configure_record_and_interrupt
description: Clears two globals, and when its index argument is nonzero it writes a 24-byte record slot through a stored pointer, selecting one of two constant words by a flag. When a second flag is set, it saves a pointer, writes the interrupt enable register with bits 15 and 14 set, and calls an unnamed routine; hardware registers touched: INTENA, INTREQ.

name: call_two_routines_in_order
description: Calls two unnamed routines in sequence and returns.

name: forward_call_to_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no other effect.

name: unrecovered_interrupt_status_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this fifteen-instruction routine, so its logic is not recovered. The listed facts show that it reads the interrupt enable and request registers and calls two other routines.

name: mask_and_store_word_field
description: Masks the data register word to bits 4 to 6 and stores it in a word field at a fixed offset from the base pointer. It then returns the first stack argument.

name: unrecovered_interrupt_control_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this twelve-instruction routine, so its logic is not recovered. The listed facts show that it touches the CIA-A interrupt control register and the interrupt request register and calls two other routines.

name: unrecovered_two_instruction_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this two-instruction routine, so its logic is not recovered. The listed facts show that one routine calls it and it calls one other routine.

name: unrecovered_one_instruction_routine
description: The decompiler produced no pseudo-code for this single-instruction routine, so its logic is not recovered. The listed facts show only that two routines call it.

name: reset_audio_scan_table
description: Scans a 128-byte table for its largest byte value and stores some global state, then zeroes the four audio volume registers and the audio control register and writes the DMA control register. Hardware registers touched: ADKCON, AUD0VOL, AUD1VOL, AUD2VOL, AUD3VOL, CIAA_PRA, DMACON.

name: build_segment_table_from_records
description: Loops over 30-byte records, computing doubled and split values from each record's word fields and writing them into a table of 16-byte entries. The loop count comes from the distance between two pointers; called by one unnamed routine.

name: update_audio_channels_per_frame
description: Increments a byte counter and, when it reaches a limit, resets it and calls an unnamed routine. It then writes the location of each of the four audio channels from per-channel records when their length field is nonzero, with short delay loops between the register writes; hardware registers touched: AUD0LCH, AUD0LEN, AUD0PER, AUD1LCH, AUD1LEN, AUD1PER, AUD2LCH, AUD2LEN, AUD2PER, AUD3LCH, AUD3LEN, AUD3PER, DMACON.

name: advance_offset_call_if_clear
description: Adds 16 to a longword at a fixed offset from the base pointer. When a flag byte at another offset is zero, it also calls four unnamed routines before returning.

name: scan_threshold_table_for_record
description: Copies a 32-bit record into a second record. Depending on the record's type nibble, it either scans a 36-word table for the first entry not above a key value, or clamps and steps a counter; it stores a pair of words into an output pointer when a field is set.

name: scale_field_by_global_factor
description: Copies a longword field, and if a masked word is nonzero and a flag byte in a table is set, it calls a routine chosen from a word table. It then stores a field equal to a global 16-bit factor times 25, times a value, divided by 1600; calls two unnamed routines.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The decompiler reports bad instruction data here, so this is not a working routine. It only truncates the control flow at that point.

name: select_table_value_mod3
description: Takes a byte argument modulo three. A zero result copies a word field, while other results shift a nibble of the data register and scan a 37-word table for the first entry not above the record's word value, storing the table value in a record field.

name: lookup_value_mod3
description: Takes a byte argument modulo three. A zero result copies a word field, while other results shift a nibble of the data register and scan a 37-word table for the first entry not above the record's word value, storing the table value in a record field.

name: scan_table_for_masked_index
description: Scans a 37-word table for the first entry not above the record's word value, then stores the table value selected by a masked index from the data register into the record's next word field.

name: copy_word_field_to_output
description: Copies one word field of its record to a second word field at a fixed offset, with no other effect.

name: scan_table_for_indexed_value
description: Scans a 37-word table for the first entry not above the record's word value, then stores the table value selected by its word argument, doubled, into a record field.

name: store_word_to_output_field
description: Stores its word argument in a fixed output field of the record.

name: subtract_and_clamp_field_minimum
description: Subtracts its word argument from a record field, raises the result to a floor of 113 when it falls below that, and copies the result to a second field.

name: adjust_level_by_nibble
description: Adjusts a level word using the high nibble of its argument: it adds that nibble with a ceiling of 64. When the nibble is zero, it subtracts the low nibble with a floor of zero instead; the result is stored in two record fields.

name: subtract_low_nibble_floor_zero
description: Subtracts the low nibble of one argument from a second word argument, floors the result at zero, and stores it in two record fields.

name: dispatch_by_high_nibble
description: Calls one of several routines selected from a word offset table by the high nibble of its argument.

name: set_bits_in_memory_partial
description: Sets bits in three memory locations and in a longword addressed through a stored pointer. The decompiler then reports bad instruction data and truncates the control flow, so the rest of the routine is not recovered; hardware registers touched: CIAA_PRA.

name: store_nonzero_word_channel
description: If a word field is nonzero, stores it in a word at a variable offset and ORs it into a second word in the base area. It then copies a longword and a word from the record into a table entry at that offset.

name: call_when_byte_zero
description: Calls one unnamed routine only when a byte at a fixed offset from the base pointer is zero.

name: call_when_byte_matches
description: Calls one unnamed routine when its byte argument matches a byte at a fixed offset from the base pointer and the word at its pointer argument is nonzero.

name: advance_counter_on_table_carry
description: If the high nibble of a byte field is nonzero, adds a table value selected by that nibble into a second byte. When the sum sets its top bit, it clears that byte, advances a longword counter that wraps to a base value at a bound, and bitwise-inverts a first byte field.

name: store_masked_five_bit_value
description: When the low five bits of its byte argument are nonzero, it stores those bits in a byte at offset 2 of the base area and clears the byte at offset 1.

name: busy_wait_count_down
description: Counts a 16-bit value down in a tight loop with no other work, which makes it a busy-wait delay. It is called by two routines.

name: unpack_backward_bitstream
description: Decodes a bit-coded stream into a buffer working backwards, emitting literal bytes or copying runs from earlier output. It obtains bits and values from helper routines, and a helper that tests a shifted flag can end the decode early.

name: read_bits_from_stream
description: Shifts bits out of a 32-bit buffer held in data registers, refilling it from a source longword when it runs empty, and accumulates bit values until a counter reaches zero. It calls a shifted-flag check and a subtraction helper.

name: raise_trap_six_stub
description: Executes trap number six, after which the decompiler reports bad instruction data and truncates the control flow. The rest of the routine is therefore not recovered.

name: unrecovered_forbid_routine

name: halt_on_nonzero_check

name: conditionally_replace_seed_pair
description: Calls an unnamed routine to obtain a 32-bit pair. When its argument register is zero, it replaces the pair with a 64-bit value from another routine, then calls a third routine for its side effects and returns the pair combined into a 64-bit result.

name: emit_segments_until_count_zero
description: Repeatedly calls unnamed routines to obtain a count and a value, advancing a running offset and emitting segment values until the remaining count reaches zero. It returns early when a helper reports a failure; calls three unnamed routines.

name: accumulate_segment_counts
description: Loops over counted segments, comparing a counter with a stored limit and adding to a count held in a stack argument. Four unnamed routines fetch and apply values until the remaining count is exhausted; it calls a one-instruction routine that clears a register.

name: copy_longs_then_bytes_rotated
description: Copies a block of longwords from a source pointer to a destination, with the count taken from a rotated copy of its argument, then copies the remaining bytes one at a time.

name: copy_longs_then_bytes
description: Copies longwords from a source pointer to a destination for a count held in the low word of the data register, then copies a short remainder byte by byte.

name: check_structure_fields
description: Compares two longword fields of a structure with a stored value. When they match and a flag field is nonzero, it returns the result of an unnamed routine; when they match and the flag is zero, it returns zero; otherwise it increments a byte field and returns zero.

name: walk_records_checking_types
description: Walks a chain of records, checking a type field and a count against values derived from a flag and a string argument. It writes two words to globals when a record matches, and returns one of several status codes, including a fixed error value for a mismatched type.

name: select_status_code_from_flag
description: Returns status code 204 unless the flag byte is not 3 and the string argument's first character is zero, in which case it returns 205.

name: walk_records_with_status_codes
description: Walks records like its sibling routine, matching a type field against a value derived from a flag and a string. It returns status code 225 for a mismatched type, 204 or 205 for other failures, and zero on success after copying a field into a global.

name: parse_df_drive_digit
description: Reads characters through an unnamed routine and checks that they spell D and F, then a digit from 0 to 3, then a colon. When they match, it stores the digit in a global.

name: stub_returns_immediately

name: copy_path_segment_to_buffer
description: Scans a string for a slash or terminator and copies the characters before it into a buffer, one at a time, through an unnamed routine. It returns a value computed from the last character and a word argument, reduced modulo 72 and offset by six, or zero when nothing was copied.

name: forward_call_result
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns its result. A branch on a flag that is always false would overwrite a global, but it never runs.

name: call_fallback_when_zero
description: Calls one unnamed routine. When its result is nonzero it returns that result; otherwise it calls a second routine and returns that result.

name: return_result_or_constant
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns its result, or the constant 405 when a zero-flag condition is not met.

name: sum_and_negate_longword_block
description: Adds 128 consecutive longwords starting at its pointer argument and returns the negated sum in the high half of the result, with the low register passed through unchanged.

name: split_position_by_eleven
description: Divides a word position by eleven to get a quotient and remainder, and combines them according to a size flag. It calls routines in a loop to step through the segments, and returns a 32-bit value combining a count and a position; calls three unnamed routines.

name: walk_512_byte_blocks
description: Stores its arguments in a stack frame and divides a position by eleven. It then calls routines in a loop, advancing an address in steps of 512 bytes per count, and returns a 64-bit result; calls three unnamed routines.

name: concat_d0_with_frame_longword
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns a 64-bit value whose high half is the data register and whose low half is a longword from the frame at a fixed offset.

name: collect_bits_from_three_probes
description: Loops three times, calling two unnamed routines on each pass. For each pass where a third routine returns minus one, it sets the result bit numbered by the loop counter, and it returns the accumulated bits.

name: probe_32_times_return_last
description: Calls one unnamed routine 32 times and returns its last result doubled, plus a carry bit from the status register.

name: store_all_ones_byte
description: Stores 255 in a global byte. The value is the bitwise OR of a mask with its complement, so it is all ones whatever the data register holds; the listed facts mention CIA port registers, but the code does not write them.

name: write_mfm_sync_and_verify
description: Loops twice, writing a preamble longword and the disk sync word into a track buffer, and calls unnamed routines to verify the result and step through the sector. It returns status 29 or 26 on failure cases and zero on success; hardware registers touched: CIAA_PRA, INTREQR; calls seven other routines.

name: scan_track_entries_for_match
description: Loops up to eleven times, calling unnamed routines to read a value and returning it on a mismatch. When a pass passes its checks, it stores a derived byte pair in the frame and returns zero; it returns 27 when the final checks fail and 24 when all eleven passes are used up.

name: validate_store_pair
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then, if a zero flag, a word comparison and two byte range checks all pass, stores a derived value in two frame words and returns zero. Otherwise it returns 27.

name: verify_track_slots
description: Loops over track slots, checking a status bit and a stored word and calling routines to compare the values read against expected ones. It returns zero on success, minus one when a status bit indicates an error, 24 or 25 for mismatches, and 27 when no matching slot is found.

name: set_bit_in_global_flag

name: wait_port_bit_clear

name: update_table_entry_with_steps

name: step_word_down_to_zero

name: spin_forever_compare_self

name: wait_while_flag_then_clear

name: restore_state_after_library_calls
description: Calls three library vector functions, the last of which the listed facts identify as exec's CloseLibrary, then restores a global from a saved copy. The listed facts also name the BEAMCON0 register, which the code does not show.

name: emit_string_table_rows
description: Walks a table of null-terminated strings, up to 22 entries, computing a destination position for each from its index with a stride of 800 bytes. It calls an unnamed routine once per character, and the table ends at a byte value of minus one.

name: store_pointer_result_global

name: scatter_bytes_stride_80
description: Copies eight bytes from a source buffer to eight destination offsets spaced 80 bytes apart, starting at offset zero, with each byte of the source going to the next offset.

name: set_fixed_global_pair

name: clear_longword_table_region
